clue.text: Ship's company held at regular intervals after son's wound

indicators.note: after says the crew and the picked letters follow the abbreviation for son

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
a ship's company is its crew

indicators.note: at regular intervals asks for every other letter of the word held, here its second and fourth

explanation.surface: A sailor's family hears that the crew were detained while a son was injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' reads as an injury, but it is the past tense of wind, as of a screw turned tight. 'at regular intervals' takes E and D from 'held'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wound tight has been twisted round and round, just as a screw is turned home.

clue.text: Perhaps capturing tailless bird — one brings it in

indicators.note: capturing says the word for perhaps surrounds the shortened bird

parts.note: say means perhaps, as in 'about, say, ten'

indicators.note: tailless means the songbird loses its last letter

parts.note: a lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: Someone guesses a bird has been caught with its tail missing by a bringer-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' trims LARK to LAR. The definition is cryptic: what a worker earns is what one 'brings in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay is earned income, money that a worker brings home each month.

clue.text: Instructions primarily crepe's prepared with?

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are rearranged
primarily means the opening letter of the word Instructions

parts.note: the 's stands for 'is', so only the word crepe is fodder

explanation.surface: Asking what directions are used in making a pancake.
explanation.walkthrough: I plus CREPE are rearranged; the whole clue also defines: a crepe is made from a set of cooking instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A cookery card lists the ingredients and method, the instructions for making a dish.

clue.text: African animal beside wet ground around lake

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation
ground is the past tense of grind, so the letters are crushed into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: An animal stands by a waterhole on soggy earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like land but signals an anagram of BESIDE WET, which goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: The wildebeest, or gnu, is an antelope of the African plains.

clue.text: Finished penning king's monotonous speech

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the word for finished surrounds the royal letter

parts.note: something finished is done
R, Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch's dull address, completed in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To drone is to talk on in a dull, humming way, so a drone is tedious talk.

clue.text: Happens to come from part of church with different conclusion

indicators.note: with different conclusion says the final letter of the church part is swapped for another

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church around the altar

explanation.surface: Something turns up by luck from a section of a church, though it ends differently.
explanation.walkthrough: The L at the end of CHANCEL is replaced with S.
explanation.definitionFit: To chance is to occur by accident, so 'chances' is a verb synonym of 'happens'.

clue.text: Growth on foot? Run out with severe cramp

indicators.note: out says the letter for run is removed from the foot growth

parts.note: a corn is a hard growth of skin on a foot
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
severe means strict

explanation.surface: A painful foot complaint and a run that ends in a harsh cramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out' reads as a cricket dismissal; the R leaves CORN to give CON.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp is to restrict or hem in, the verb meaning to squeeze tight.

clue.text: Criticism rarely holds up fighting

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the hidden letters read from bottom to top
holds says the answer sits within the words Criticism rarely

explanation.surface: A combatant seldom draws criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms means weapons and, by extension, warfare, as in 'a call to arms'.

clue.text: Prisoner with court attendee — one will try to deceive you

definitions.text: one will try to deceive you

parts.note: con is short for convict
a juror attends court to hear a trial

explanation.surface: A convict sits beside a juror who may try to fool him.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage magician performs tricks designed to fool and mislead an audience.

clue.text: South American writers start to exhibit tension

parts.note: pens are writing instruments

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the word exhibit is taken

explanation.surface: Authors from South America begin to show strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the anxious uncertainty of waiting for an outcome, a state of tension.

clue.text: Healthy drinks served here?

parts.note: read 'healthy' as 'generous', as in a healthy measure: generous drinks are poured at the neighbourhood pub

explanation.surface: It sounds like a health-food bar serving smoothies.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is the pub nearest your home, where a healthy (generous) drink is poured, not a wholesome one.
explanation.definitionFit: The neighbourhood pub, where people go for a drink, is called the local in British speech.

clue.text: Doctor sent Tom in for medicinal creams

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A GP sends a patient called Tom off to the chemist for creams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person prescribing, but it is the verb meaning to alter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ointments are greasy preparations applied to the skin as medicine, so they fit medicinal creams.

clue.text: Deputises for The Queen, returning gifts

indicators.note: returning means the two letters for the Queen are read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword abbreviation for the Queen
gifts are presents

explanation.surface: Someone stands in for the monarch and hands back the presents.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise for someone is to act on their behalf, which is to stand as their representative.

clue.text: We're told beach is safe

indicators.note: we're told signals that a word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a beach is the shore

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers are assured the beach is safe for swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: In many British accents the word for the coast and the word for certain sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A safe bet is a certain one, so safe can mean certain or reliable.

clue.text: Tone from cash machine: two rings?

parts.note: ATM is an automated teller machine
O is a ring shape and sphere means a circle, as in a sphere or ring of influence

explanation.surface: A cash machine's beep, with a question about a phone ringing twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tone' and 'rings' suggest telephones, but O and SPHERE are the two circles, the question mark owning up to the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: The mood or feel of a place, as in the tone of a meeting, is its prevailing air.

clue.text: Tailor contrite with sir's ties

indicators.note: to tailor is to cut and fit, so the letters of the following words are reshaped

explanation.surface: An apologetic tailor deals with a gentleman's neckties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor' reads as the outfitter but is the verb, rearranging CONTRITE plus SIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ties in the sense of constraints or bonds are limits placed on someone's freedom.

clue.text: Changing train — do it for practice

indicators.note: changing means altering the order of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Passengers told to change trains for the practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing train' looks like a commuter's move but signals an anagram of TRAIN DO IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is an established custom, a practice handed down.

clue.text: Esther half-ignored one friend's opinion

indicators.note: half-ignored means the back three letters of the name Esther are dropped, keeping the front half

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a mate is a friend; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: Esther was half overlooked in a friend's view.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is a judgment or rough assessment, so a considered view or opinion.

clue.text: Tries raising volunteers with invites

indicators.note: raising in a down clue lifts the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
to invite trouble is to tempt it

explanation.surface: Recruiters try to draw in volunteers by sending invitations.
explanation.definitionFit: Attempts are efforts to do something, so they are tries.

clue.text: School test — is rebellious group getting pleasure?

parts.note: the SAT is an American school examination
a faction is a dissenting group within a party

explanation.surface: A teacher wonders whether a group of pupils is enjoying defying an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfaction is the contentment or gratification felt when a wish is met, close to pleasure.

clue.text: Confusion no good in middle of story

indicators.note: in middle of says the abbreviation goes inside the word for story

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A muddled bit of plot that is useless in the heart of a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle is a muddle or mix-up, a state of confusion.

clue.text: Look — a second domesticated animal catches cold

indicators.note: catches means the animal holds the letter for cold inside it

parts.note: a pet is a domesticated animal
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Glance quickly: another pet has caught a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is the appearance or look of something, as in a building's aspect.

clue.text: I highly valued no Republican belief

indicators.note: no says the letter for the party is left out of the word for precious

parts.note: something dear is highly valued

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they never prized the Republican creed.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can be a notion or opinion that someone holds, which is a belief.

clue.text: Drunk, pa's despair vanishes

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A father, inebriated, sees his gloom melt away.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to go out of sight, a direct synonym of the verb for going out of view.

clue.text: Declare area good in street in Paris

indicators.note: in says the letter for good goes inside the French street

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: Someone announces a fine district on a Parisian boulevard.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue can mean to maintain or assert a case, so to state firmly or declare.

clue.text: Dead slow

definitions.meaning: the ... so-and-so means someone who has died
behind time or tardy, as a train running behind

explanation.definitionFit: Late means deceased in 'the late king' and behind schedule when describing a train.

clue.text: Winning — something a cricketer might be doing?

definitions.meaning: winning in the sense of charming or attractive

definitions.text: something a cricketer might be doing?
definitions.meaning: fielders in cricket call out to the umpire asking for a batsman to be given out

explanation.surface: A winning streak seems to belong to a cricketer pleading with the umpire.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fielders shout 'Howzat?' to appeal to the umpire for a wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: A winning smile is a charming one, and charming means attractive or pleasing.

clue.text: Dog ignoring black bird

indicators.note: ignoring says the letter for black is dropped from the hound

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A dog pays no attention to a dark bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Oriental cuisine's finale: a small bird

indicators.note: finale means the closing letter of the word for cooking style is taken

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: An Asian meal ends with a little bird as its last course.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means of the East, so the two are synonyms for things from Asia.

clue.text: Piece from singer Fitzgerald intended to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard signals that the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: Ella Fitzgerald was the American jazz singer; intended means meant

explanation.surface: A song by Ella Fitzgerald is meant for listening.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is a component or part of a whole, so a piece of something.
